// diagnostic

E0142

`#SingleUse` value lent/shared instead of moved (D-LIN1)

What

`#SingleUse` value lent/shared instead of moved (D-LIN1)

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E0142

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0142: tests/ui/loop_borrowed_task_list.stderr.

Error [E0120]: `hs` was not moved here, so this loop can't take its handles
  --> tests/ui/loop_borrowed_task_list.jet:3:15
    |
  3 |     loop h in hs -> total += h.join() ?? 0
    |               ^^
 Why: each step hands you the handle itself, and a task handle cannot be copied — so the loop takes the whole list with the move marker `^`
 Fix: take the list with the move marker `^`: `hs: ^[Task<Int>]`, or collect the work in a canonical `task.all` or `task.group` block
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0120

Error [E0142]: `handles` can't be shared — it must be used exactly once
  --> tests/ui/loop_borrowed_task_list.jet:9:17
    |
  9 |     print(drain(handles))
    |                 ^^^^^^^
 Why: this value's type is `#SingleUse`, so it can only be moved (handed over for good); `drain` would borrow or copy it, and a `#SingleUse` value has no second use to give
 Fix: move it with the move marker `^` (`^handles`) to give it away, or rework the call so it takes ownership through that marker
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0142

Error [E0142]: `handles` can't be shared — it must be used exactly once
  --> tests/ui/loop_borrowed_task_list.jet:9:17
    |
  9 |     print(drain(handles))
    |                 ^^^^^^^
 Why: this value's type is `#SingleUse`, so it can only be moved (handed over for good); `drain` would borrow or copy it, and a `#SingleUse` value has no second use to give
 Fix: move it with the move marker `^` (`^handles`) to give it away, or rework the call so it takes ownership through that marker

Error [E0140]: `handles` still owes `consume`
  --> tests/ui/loop_borrowed_task_list.jet:8:5
    |
  8 |     handles :: [task 1, task 2]
    |     ^^^^^^^
 Why: this value's type is `#SingleUse`, so it carries a job that has to be done — dropping it without doing that job leaves the work undone (an unjoined task, an unreleased lock)
 Fix: consume it exactly once: move it to a parameter with the move marker `^`, or `return` it — or write `#Unsafe("reason") { consume(handles) }` to discard it deliberately
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0140
